summary.headline: Time Technoplast Q1 FY27 net sales rose 25% to INR1,694 crore and PAT 22% to INR116 crore, with volume up 11%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 net sales rose 25% YoY to INR1,694 crore (India +30%, overseas +17%) on 11% volume growth, while EBITDA rose 15% to INR225 crore and PAT rose 22% to INR116 crore. Management said the India-overseas revenue gap reflects differing fiscal and calendar year reporting, with overseas consolidated on a calendar basis. Net debt fell by INR90 crore and operating cash flow was INR155 crore, with capex of INR75 crore. Management kept its volume growth target of above 15% but declined to give EBITDA percentage guidance while polymer prices remain volatile due to the West Asia conflict.

financial_highlights.change: INR28 crore maintenance and expansion for established products; INR47 crore for IBC and composite cylinders

financial_highlights.value: INR9 crore realised of INR134 crore identified

segments.name: Packaging (industrial)
segments.commentary: Management cites about 75% of revenue as polymer-based packaging; FY27 growth guidance 11-13%. Management said India and overseas each account for roughly 37% of total revenue within packaging.

segments.name: Composite products
segments.commentary: Growth of 29.3% in Q1; FY27 guidance 25-30%. Order book about INR185 crore; composite products carry EBITDA margins around 18%, per management.

segments.name: PE pipes
segments.commentary: Q1 volumes were subdued because EPC contractors did not get price increases from government and the company held back supply; FY27 guidance above 20-25%. Management expects about 75% capacity utilisation in August-September.

segments.name: Power Build Batteries (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Business about INR125 crore, targeting over 30% growth for at least 3 years and EBITDA margin rising from 12% to 15% in two years, under a tie-up with Monbat (Europe).

guidance_outlook: Volume growth guided above 15% for FY27; management said it is not changing growth guidance, but revenue growth depends on polymer prices.
If volume grows 15%, management expects EBITDA growth of 19-20% and PAT growth of 23-24%; EBITDA percentage guidance withheld until prices stabilise.
Management cited a reasonable EBITDA margin range of 14-15.5% if polymer prices settle at $1,100-1,250/ton with oil at $70-80/barrel.
Working capital cycle was 115 days in March 2026, about 110 days now; target 100 days by year-end and 90 days over 2-3 years.
ROCE to rise about 1.75% a year, reaching about 24% in three years from 19% in March 2026.
Capex of about INR350 crore in FY26-27 combined; thereafter normal capex of INR200-250 crore a year, including INR100 crore maintenance.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation about 80% in India and 85% overseas; US (Georgia) above 90%, operating in 5 states with 6 more under implementation.
LPG cylinder capacity 1.4 million cylinders; maximum output 12.5 lakh cylinders a year; HPCL order for 140,000 cylinders.
Fully automatic composite plant at Mouda completed; Silvassa IBC automation Phase 1 done, Phase 2 under implementation; Gummidipoondi pipe facility operational.
Acquisition of a small company in Dhule (PE pipes, INR25 crore investment) completed; commercial production from Q2. Ebullient Packaging acquisition pending on terms and war stabilisation.
Saudi Arabia plant building to be completed in about a month; machinery commissioning depends on the war situation. Planned new sites include Sanand (Gujarat), Odisha, and Chiplun (Maharashtra).
demand_pricing: Pricing is monthly, with customers' revisions effective on dates between the 8th and 12th of the following month; management says 70-75% of customers follow this, and packaging is about 6-7% of customers' cost.
Polymer prices rose through April-June and fell from July; management says a INR23 decline was followed by a INR6 increase, so net INR17 is being passed on in the current month.
Composite orders are on fixed pricing with about six months of inventory carried and input costs fixed for 12 months, per management.
Consumer demand for PE pipes is weaker because government did not raise EPC contractor prices; August-September demand is improving.
LPG cylinder exports and domestic sales are about 50-50 in normal years; domestic supply is entirely to PSU oil marketing companies.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days have worsened and cash flow is flat; how will surplus cash of INR600-700 crore be deployed, including inorganic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle rose to 115 days in March 2026 due to a 25-30% raw material price spike, and is now about 110 days with a 100-day year-end target and 90-day long-term target. Surplus cash could go to organic or inorganic growth, buybacks from FY27 onwards, or higher payout ratio, subject to board and SEBI rules.

qa_highlights.question: How has the polymer price increase been passed through to customers, and is there more to pass on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most price increases from March and April were fully passed on and the company uses monthly pricing with a 20-25 day lag. Polymer price movements since July have been netted into the current month's prices.

qa_highlights.question: Q1 PE pipe volumes were subdued; is this timing or a shift to the second half?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slowdown was from EPC contractors not receiving government price increases, and the company held back supply rather than absorb the loss. Management expects about 75% capacity use in August-September and PE pipe sales to be 35-40% in H1 and 60-65% in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What crude price gives the best margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees polymer at $1,100-1,250 per ton and crude at $70-80 per barrel as reasonable, which would support EBITDA margin of 14-15.5%. It focuses on absolute EBITDA per tonne, not percentage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic vs export split for LPG cylinders and the PSU exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic and export are roughly 50-50 normally, with 50-60% of orders taken from local demand first; domestic supply is entirely to PSU companies.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income low given INR342 crore of unutilised QIP funds, and what is the finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the QIP funds sit in fixed deposits with interest netted against finance cost, so other income is small (about INR1 crore in Q1, mainly rentals). Cost of funds is about 8.5% in India and 6.5% overseas; finance cost is now around INR35-40 crore a year, mostly non-fund-based costs such as bank guarantees (INR400-500 crore utilised).

risks_watch: Polymer price volatility from the West Asia conflict; margin and working capital swings with input prices.
Government and EPC contractor pricing for PE pipes; the company may hold back supply when prices are not raised.
Ebullient Packaging acquisition: terms not agreed; company is 60% export and exposed to Middle East disruption. Board may redeploy the funds if terms are not met.
Capex of about INR350 crore, with QIP proceeds of about INR342 crore unutilised and held in FDs; deployment timing and returns to be tracked.
Non-core asset sales: INR125 crore left to realise of INR134 crore.
Solar-power savings (INR12 crore this year; up to INR35 crore possible) depend on state policies, which management says are uncertain.
Fire extinguisher and CNG 250/350-litre cylinder approvals expected within about 90 days; fire extinguisher volumes expected in H2.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and order visibility, but cautious on margins and EBITDA guidance, which management tied to polymer price stabilisation. Answers on finance cost and other income were long and partly unclear, and management deferred some detail to a follow-up with the CFO.
